Reduce each geometry to one representative point

Source: R/crs-geometry.R
coerce_to_points.Rd

Replaces the geometry of each row of an sf object with a point, by the rule mode names. The result has one row per row of x, in the same order.

Usage

coerce_to_points(
  x,
  mode = c("auto", "centroid", "point_on_surface", "surface", "line_midpoint",
    "bbox_center"),
  tmp_project = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

An sf object.

mode

How each geometry becomes a point: "auto" (default), "centroid", "point_on_surface", "surface" (an alias for "point_on_surface"), "line_midpoint" or "bbox_center". See "Modes".

tmp_project

Logical; take line midpoints in a temporary projection. Default TRUE. With FALSE, lines in longitude and latitude get their centroid. When x has no CRS and the lon/lat test of ensure_projected() takes its coordinates for degrees, the temporary projection reads them as EPSG:4326 (with a warning), and the midpoints returned are geodesic ones brought back to the input's numbers, not planar midpoints. Set the CRS, or pass tmp_project = FALSE, for planar data.

Value

An sf object with its geometry reduced to POINTs, row for row with x; an empty input geometry gives an empty POINT.

Modes

"auto" (default)

POINT rows are kept. POLYGON and MULTIPOLYGON rows get a point on the surface. A LINESTRING gets its midpoint, and a MULTILINESTRING the midpoint of its longest part (see "Lines"). MULTIPOINT rows and rows of other types, such as geometry collections, get their centroid.

"centroid"

The centroid of every row.

"point_on_surface" (alias "surface")

A point that lies on each geometry, taken with GEOS.

"line_midpoint"

The midpoint of each LINESTRING, taken in a temporary projection (with tmp_project = FALSE on lon/lat data, its centroid). Rows of other types (points, polygons and their MULTI forms) get their centroid. A MULTILINESTRING or GEOMETRYCOLLECTION row is an error: cast it to LINESTRING first, or use "auto", which takes the midpoint of a MULTILINESTRING's longest part.

"bbox_center"

The centre of each row's bounding box.

Empty geometries and rows without a location

An empty geometry of any type, lines included, becomes an empty POINT in its own row; prep_model_data() and make_folds() then drop such rows, as they drop any other empty geometry. An empty part inside a non-empty feature is ignored, so the feature gets the point its other parts give.

A geometry with no location (see spatialkit-geometry, "Rows without a location") gets an empty POINT in every mode, as an empty geometry does. So does a geometry of a layer in a geographic CRS with a vertex at a latitude beyond 90 degrees, and a warning of class spatialkit_lat_beyond_90 gives its rows of x (rows).

Lines

Modes "auto" and "line_midpoint" take the midpoint of a line in a temporary projection (tmp_project), the one ensure_projected() chooses for the lines. A line that projection returns empty or without some of its vertices is not sampled: the call stops with an error of class spatialkit_features_degenerate (see "Errors").

In mode "auto" a MULTILINESTRING gets the midpoint of its longest part. When several parts share the greatest length (to one part in ten million, measured in the projection used), their midpoints are taken and the one lowest in x, then in y, is kept, so the point does not depend on the order in which the feature lists its parts. x values within one part in ten million of the diagonal of the midpoints' bounding box count as one, so y decides between midpoints whose x differ only in their last bits, and the point does not move with the origin of the coordinates.

Longitude and latitude

Modes "auto" (for polygons) and "point_on_surface" take the point with GEOS, which reads a layer in longitude and latitude on the plane in degrees, under either sf::sf_use_s2() setting. sf's warning that such a point "may not give correct results for longitude/latitude data" is not passed on. A polygon that spans more than 180 degrees of longitude (one written across longitude 180, from 179.5 to -179.5) GEOS reads the long way round the globe, so its point is tested on the polygon read on the sphere with s2; when it does not lie on it, the point is taken again with the longitudes below 0 read from 180 to 360, and brought back into -180 to 180. A polygon whose point lies on it neither way, or that s2 cannot read, keeps GEOS's point, and a warning of class spatialkit_surface_point_off gives its rows of x (rows). When x has no CRS and the lon/lat test of ensure_projected() takes its coordinates for degrees, its polygons that span more than 180 units are read so too, as EPSG:4326, and a warning names the rows whose point that reading moves; the points keep the missing CRS.

Mode "bbox_center", and the centroids that GEOS takes on the plane in degrees (a lon/lat layer with s2 off) under "centroid", for the rows other than LINESTRINGs under "line_midpoint", and for MULTIPOINTs and collections under "auto", read a geometry written across longitude 180 the same way: one that spans more than 180 degrees of longitude as written, and no more than 180 with the longitudes below 0 read from 180 to 360, gets the centre of that box, or GEOS's centroid of the geometry so read, brought back into -180 to 180. A layer without a CRS that the lon/lat test takes for degrees is read so too, with the same warning. A geometry wider than 180 degrees in both readings, such as one around a pole, keeps the centre of its box on the plane, or GEOS's planar centroid. The centroids s2 takes on the sphere are not changed.

With s2 on, sf takes the centroids of a lon/lat layer with s2 (under "centroid", for the rows other than LINESTRINGs under "line_midpoint", and for collections under "auto"), and s2 refuses some polygons GEOS accepts. A polygon s2 refuses because a vertex repeats the one before it, on its own or inside a collection, gets the centroid of the same ring without the repeat; the ring's points are unchanged. A polygon s2 refuses for another reason (edges that cross, a figure eight) is an error (see "Errors"). With s2 off, the centroids are GEOS's, planar in degrees.

Z and M coordinates

A layer whose geometries do not all have the same dimensions (XY beside XYZ or XYM, as rbind() of an XY and an XYZ layer gives) is read in x and y, and its points come back in XY with a warning of class spatialkit_zm_dropped whose rows are the rows that carried Z or M (see spatialkit-geometry, "Mixed dimensions, Z and M"). A layer in one dimension, XY or XYZ throughout, is read as it is, and so is a layer whose only geometries of another dimension than the first are empty and not points.

GEOS does not read M coordinates. When the mode reduces a geometry that carries M (XYM or XYZM) to a point (any such geometry under "centroid", "point_on_surface" and "line_midpoint", any that is not a POINT under "auto"), the layer is reduced in x and y: Z and M are dropped from every geometry, the points come back in XY, and a warning of class spatialkit_zm_dropped says so, with the rows whose geometry carries M as its rows. Empty geometries are not counted. A POINT layer that carries M is returned as it is under "auto". Mode "bbox_center" reads the box of each geometry and gives XY points for any layer, with no warning about Z or M.

Errors

Each of these is an error of class spatialkit_features_degenerate that gives the rows of x (rows on the condition):

A polygon s2 refuses

In longitude and latitude with s2 on, a polygon whose centroid s2 cannot take even without its repeated vertices. The message quotes s2 and says to transform x to a projected CRS or to use another mode.

A centroid outside its feature

GEOS, which takes the centroids in a projected CRS, without a CRS, and in degrees with s2 off, weights each part of a ring by its signed area. Where the edges of a ring cross (a bowtie), or a hole lies outside its shell, parts of the feature count with opposite signs, and the point can lie far outside the feature. A centroid outside the bounding box of a feature GEOS reports invalid is refused: the condition carries site = "geos_centroid" and GEOS's reason for each row (reasons), and the message says to pass mode = "point_on_surface" or to repair the features with sf::st_make_valid(). A centroid inside the box is returned as GEOS gives it.

A line the temporary projection cannot place

A line that the projection returns empty or without some of its vertices. The condition carries site = "projection", and the message says to pass mode = "centroid" or tmp_project = FALSE, which take the point in longitude and latitude, without the projection.

The functions that reduce a layer they are given to points this way (prep_model_data(), make_folds(), fold_separation(), estimate_sac_range(), resolution_profile(), determine_optimal_levels(), cell_values_at(), summarize_by_cell(), select_features_forward(), compare_models_cv(), area_of_applicability(), predict_surface()) raise each of these errors in their own name, with the same class and fields, naming their argument and its rows. spatialkit-conditions lists every class.

See also

spatialkit-geometry for how input geometry and CRSs are read.

Other data preparation: [.spatialkit_rows(), ensure_projected(), harmonize_crs(), prep_model_data(), spatialkit-geometry

Examples

library(sf)
poly <- st_sf(
  id = 1,
  geometry = st_sfc(st_polygon(list(rbind(
    c(0, 0), c(2, 0), c(2, 2), c(0, 2), c(0, 0)
  ))), crs = 32632)
)
coerce_to_points(poly, "auto")  # a point on the polygon's surface
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 1 field
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1 ymin: 1 xmax: 1 ymax: 1
#> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / UTM zone 32N
#>   id    geometry
#> 1  1 POINT (1 1)
